It addresses the difficulty of simultaneously optimizing complex geometry, texture, and non-rigid deformation from scratch by either decaying the weight of a coarse reconstruction loss relative to a fine-grained loss [S1] or by annealing the frequency components of the positional encoding used by the deformation network [S2].

The claim states that the evidence supports two methods for addressing the difficulty of simultaneous optimization: 1) decaying the weight of a coarse reconstruction loss relative to a fine-grained loss [S1], and 2) annealing the frequency components of the positional encoding [S2]. Source [S1] explicitly mentions a 'coarse-to-fine optimization strategy' using an 'exponentially decaying weight' to balance coarse and fine RGB reconstruction losses, addressing the difficulty of simultaneous optimization from scratch due to complex geometry and texture. Source [S2] explicitly proposes a 'coarse-to-fine optimization scheme' that 'modulates the components of the input positional encoding... by frequency' to avoid local minima and refine deformations. Both parts of the claim are directly supported by the provided text.
